newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SHOCKED BY FEDERATION CHIEF'S MURDER.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SHOCKED BY FEDERATION CHIEF'S MURDER.

text.p: Russia's ice hockey squad are in shock after the murder of federation chief Valentin Sych on the eve of the World championships but are confident they can at least reach the semifinals.

Federation spokesman Mikhail Govorkov told Reuters that Sych's death in an apparent contract killing on Tuesday had demoralised the team and was partly to blame for a 7-1 defeat in a friendly match against Finland in Helsinki on Tuesday.
"However, the team is still thinking positively and we think it can perform well enough in this championship," Govorkov said, referring to the World Cup starting in Helsinki on Saturday.
He said he still believed Russia could count at least on a semifinal place.
But Russia's problems are piling up.
Team officials said earlier this month that success would depend on how many of their foreign-based players would be available.
But Govorkov said only Andrei Nikolishin, who plays for the Washington Capitals, nd Dmitry Yushkevich of the Toronto Maple Leafs were certainly coming to Finland.
"Two places will be reserved for more NHL players, but we do not yet know who they might be," Govorkov said.
At least Russian-based forward Alexei Gorshkov and defence Dmitry Krasotkin have joined the squad from Torpedo Yaroslavl, Russia's newly-crowned league champions, after the domestic play-offs.
Big hopes are pinned on Sweden-based sniper Vyacheslav Butsayev.

Other Russians to watch are defencemen Sergei Fokin and Sergei Bautin who play in Sweden, Dmitry Yerofeyev and forward Alexander Prokopyev of Czech team Vitkowitse, Anatoly Fedotov and Alexander Barkov of Finland's Tappara and Alexander Kharitonov of Dynamo Moscow.
The Soviet Union once dominated ice hockey but Russia have rarely tasted glory since the Soviet empire collapsed in 1991.
Many of their top players have gone abroad and Russia last won a world championship in 1993, under coach Boris Mikhailov.
